summary.oneLiner: Leading Indian manufacturer of specialty Oleo Chemicals (fatty acids) and intermediate nutraceuticals, holding a leadership position in Dimer Acid and the only Indian maker of paint-grade Linoleic Acid and Isostearic Acid.
summary.business: Fairchem Organics manufactures specialty Oleo Chemicals - principally Dimer Acid, Linoleic Acid / Soya Fatty Acid, Isostearic Acid, Monobasic Acid, Palmitic Acid and other Distilled Fatty Acids - by processing by-products of vegetable-oil refineries into higher-grade fatty acids. It also produces (natural) Tocopherols and Sterols, intermediate nutraceuticals that are exclusively exported. It operates a Business-to-Business model, selling to manufacturers of epoxy hardeners, paints, printing inks, adhesives, lubricants, cosmetics, soaps, animal feed, pet food and pharma products.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and import dependence
risks.note: Management flags availability of the right kinds of raw materials in adequate quantity at fair prices as the main risk; raw materials are by-products of vegetable-oil refineries, and India depends substantially on imports of crude vegetable oils from Indonesia, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Ukraine and Russia, so those countries' export-policy shifts or events such as war can spike raw-material prices that are difficult to pass through to finished-product pricing quickly.

risks.risk: Product concentration in three core products
risks.note: Dimer Acid, Linoleic Acid and Isostearic Acid together contributed 73.1% of value during the year, and the products/services sold table shows a single product line (specialty oleo chemicals) accounting for 94.20% of turnover, so performance is highly sensitive to demand and margin swings in this narrow product set.

Demand moderation from customers was attributed to continual macro uncertainty from U.S.A. tariffs to the recent Middle East war crisis, indicating export and customer demand is exposed to global trade-policy and geopolitical shocks.
Internal control disclosures note the Company operates with a single operational location, concentrating manufacturing, regulatory and operational risk at one site.

Identified as one of the categories in the Company's formal Risk Management Policy; relevant given the Company's export revenue (7.80% of turnover in FY2025-26) and stated ambition to grow exports further.

The Board's Risk Management Policy separately identifies Country specific Risk and Information/Cyber Security Risk, among others (Business, Technological, Financial, Liquidity, Safety, Employee and Natural Calamity risks), as factors that in the Board's opinion could threaten the Company's existence.

one-line thesis: Fairchem Organics has bottomed out in Q4FY26 as Chinese dumping abated and paint demand recovered, driving a margin rebound to 6.9% despite a 3.2% revenue decline. The core investment thesis pivots on restoring 80% capacity utilization in FY27 and the phased commissioning (FY27-28) of a novel high-margin product line targeting $1B+ revenue potential over five years.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs. 117cr (Q4, -3.2% YoY), Rs. 460cr (FY26, -14.5% YoY); EBITDA: Rs. 8cr (Q4, margin 6.9%), Rs. 22cr (FY26, margin 4.8%); PAT: Rs. 3.7cr (Q4 adj), Rs. 6.2cr (FY26); Order Book: Not disclosed (market-driven spot sales); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but capex deferred to preserve balance sheet. One-offs: Power/fuel cost savings of Rs. 20cr annually due to energy audit; Buyback of 4.25 lakh shares completed.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Targeting 75-80% capacity utilization in FY27 (vs 65% in FY26); Margin: Targeting 8% EBITDA in FY27, potential for double-digits long-term; Order Inflow: Export share to rise from 9% to 20% in 12-14 months; Capex: Minimal in FY27 (only energy savings), major capex for new product phased over 5 years.
order book & pipeline: No formal order book; sales are spot/monthly contracts. Demand visibility improving with Chinese import pressure easing (imports dropped from ~1000 tonnes/month to negligible).
segment / subsidiary detail: Dimer Acid: ~30% of revenue (Rs. 140cr); Linoleic Acid: ~30% of revenue; Isosteric Acid: ~5-6% (Rs. 26cr), high-margin cosmetic grade with long validation cycle; Bypass Fat: New plant operational next month (Q1FY27), revenue from Q3FY27.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Capacity utilization ramp-up from 65% to 95% over 2 years on existing 80kT plant. 2) New novel oleochemical product (40kT potential capacity) commissioning Q2FY27, targeting Rs. 800-1000cr revenue over 5 years with 15-18% margins. 3) Export expansion to US/EU/Japan leveraging FTAs and rupee depreciation.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% in Q4 (vs 3.6% in Q4FY25) driven by 8-10% price realization gain due to reduced Chinese dumping and energy cost savings (Rs. 60cr in Q4 vs Rs. 80cr prior year). Raw material (vegetable oil) prices stable; power/fuel costs down due to equipment upgrades.
capex / expansion: FY27: Negligible except for energy efficiency projects (payback <4 years). New product line: Initial Rs. 20-25cr deployed for 8kT phase, expanding to 40kT over 5 years based on demand validation.
capital allocation: Share buyback completed (Rs. 4.25 lakh shares, promoter holding up to 63.2%). Dividend reduced to Rs. 1/share (vs Rs. 7.5 last year) due to temporary earnings dip. Future capex to be funded internally/debt only upon new product revenue traction.
risks & watch-items: 1) Resumption of Chinese dumping if export incentives reintroduced. 2) Volatility in vegetable oil prices (daily revision contracts). 3) Delay in customer validation for new high-margin product (2-2.5 year cycle). 4) Working capital strain (cycle at 100-120 days).
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledged 'washed out' last two years but emphasized structural turnaround via dumping cessation and operational efficiencies. Confident on 8% margin target and long-term vision.
non-obvious takeaways: Management revealed that Chinese dumping ceased likely due to removal of 15% export incentives by Beijing, not just market forces. Also, the new 40kT capacity is not a single block but will be ramped gradually (starting 8kT) to match slow customer validation cycles in cosmetics/specialty sectors.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chinese dumping of dimer acid has ceased, allowing domestic players to regain pricing power and volume. | Fairchem Organics Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of 8-10% price recovery and volume ramp-up; margins expanding from 4.8% to targeted 8%+. |
| Paint industry recovery and reduced import pressure benefit upstream additive suppliers. | Asian Paints | beneficiary | Med | Stable supply chain and potential cost pass-through benefits, though Fairchem is a small supplier relative to Asian Paints' scale. |
| High vegetable oil prices and import duties squeeze margins for edible oil refiners. | Adani Wilmar | loser | Low | While Adani Wilmar integrates forward, their core refining business faces raw material cost pressure; Fairchem notes raw material is commodity-priced daily. |

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

hero.oneLiner: Leading Indian manufacturer of specialty Oleo Chemicals (fatty acids) and intermediate nutraceuticals, holding a leadership position in Dimer Acid and the only Indian maker of paint-grade Linoleic Acid and Isostearic Acid.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Leading Indian manufacturer of specialty Oleo Chemicals (fatty acids) and intermediate nutraceuticals, holding a leadership position in Dimer Acid and the only Indian maker of paint-grade Linoleic Acid and Isostearic Acid.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Fairchem Organics manufactures specialty Oleo Chemicals - principally Dimer Acid, Linoleic Acid / Soya Fatty Acid, Isostearic Acid, Monobasic Acid, Palmitic Acid and other Distilled Fatty Acids - by processing by-products of vegetable-oil refineries into higher-grade fatty acids. It also produces (natural) Tocopherols and Sterols, intermediate nutraceuticals that are exclusively exported. It operates a Business-to-Business model, selling to manufacturers of epoxy hardeners, paints, printing inks, adhesives, lubricants, cosmetics, soaps, animal feed, pet food and pharma products.

segment_detail.body: Dimer Acid: ~30% of revenue (Rs. 140cr); Linoleic Acid: ~30% of revenue; Isosteric Acid: ~5-6% (Rs. 26cr), high-margin cosmetic grade with long validation cycle; Bypass Fat: New plant operational next month (Q1FY27), revenue from Q3FY27.

products.body:

- **Intermediate Nutraceuticals:** Tocopherols, Sterols

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Paints and printing inks (via Alkyd Resin / Polyamide intermediates)
- Adhesives, paper coatings, marine and construction surface coatings
- Oil drilling operations
- Lubricants and cosmetics
- Pet food, pharmaceutical and cosmetics (via natural Vitamin E / Sterols)
- Soaps and animal feed
- Domestic market across 21 states
- Export markets across 12 countries (exports were 7.80% of total turnover in FY2025-26)

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:
- ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management)
- ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental Management)
- ISO 45001:2018 (Occupational Health and Safety Management)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: No formal order book; sales are spot/monthly contracts. Demand visibility improving with Chinese import pressure easing (imports dropped from ~1000 tonnes/month to negligible).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting 75-80% capacity utilization in FY27 (vs 65% in FY26); Margin: Targeting 8% EBITDA in FY27, potential for double-digits long-term; Order Inflow: Export share to rise from 9% to 20% in 12-14 months; Capex: Minimal in FY27 (only energy savings), major capex for new product phased over 5 years.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 1) Capacity utilization ramp-up from 65% to 95% over 2 years on existing 80kT plant. 2) New novel oleochemical product (40kT potential capacity) commissioning Q2FY27, targeting Rs. 800-1000cr revenue over 5 years with 15-18% margins. 3) Export expansion to US/EU/Japan leveraging FTAs and rupee depreciation.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for biodegradable chemicals from natural sources is supporting growth of the oleo chemicals market
- Rising demand from printing inks, adhesives and paper-coatings industries expected to drive demand for non-reactive polyamide (Dimer Acid) applications
- Increasing surface-coatings and adhesives demand in marine and construction expected to drive reactive-polyamide applications
- FY2025-26 performance was impacted by higher raw material cost not fully passed through to finished-product pricing, and by demand moderation from customers amid macro uncertainty from U.S.A. tariffs and the Middle East war crisis
- Management is 'consciously optimistic' about FY2026-27 export competitiveness due to lower U.S. tariffs, a likely FTA with the UK and EU, and recent rupee devaluation
- India's dependence on imported crude vegetable oils (from Indonesia, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Ukraine, Russia) exposes raw-material pricing to those countries' export policy shifts and geopolitical disruption

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% in Q4 (vs 3.6% in Q4FY25) driven by 8-10% price realization gain due to reduced Chinese dumping and energy cost savings (Rs. 60cr in Q4 vs Rs. 80cr prior year). Raw material (vegetable oil) prices stable; power/fuel costs down due to equipment upgrades.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Share buyback completed (Rs. 4.25 lakh shares, promoter holding up to 63.2%). Dividend reduced to Rs. 1/share (vs Rs. 7.5 last year) due to temporary earnings dip. Future capex to be funded internally/debt only upon new product revenue traction.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: No new plant, line or capacity-expansion project with a commissioning/completion timeline is disclosed in this bundle. The Company successfully launched its in-house developed, high-value Isostearic Acid product in the international market during the year, with an encouraging initial response. As part of its environmental strategy it continues to implement a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system to capture, treat and reuse all water and liquid waste generated by operations, supported by targeted capex investment aimed at resource efficiency and reduced water consumption; solid-waste management from production processes has also been improved.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledged 'washed out' last two years but emphasized structural turnaround via dumping cessation and operational efficiencies. Confident on 8% margin target and long-term vision.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leadership position in the Indian Dimer Acid market, built on pricing strategy, timely service, quick supply, fair payment terms and quality, against Chinese suppliers as main competitors
- Ability to process by-products with no fixed technical specification into higher-grade fatty acids and intermediate nutraceuticals meeting stringent quality standards
- Strong, long-standing customer and supplier relationships of more than 25 years
- First Indian and reportedly first Asian company to manufacture Isostearic Acid to internationally acceptable quality without importing technology or external consultants, in a field with only 3-4 global manufacturers
- Only Indian company producing the grade of Linoleic Acid needed for superior-grade paints, making it the preferred supplier for that use
- Natural structural barrier to new entrants: limited domestic availability of key raw materials and unviable import economics under prevailing duties make the market suited to essentially one large domestic player

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Resumption of Chinese dumping if export incentives reintroduced. 2) Volatility in vegetable oil prices (daily revision contracts). 3) Delay in customer validation for new high-margin product (2-2.5 year cycle). 4) Working capital strain (cycle at 100-120 days).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management revealed that Chinese dumping ceased likely due to removal of 15% export incentives by Beijing, not just market forces. Also, the new 40kT capacity is not a single block but will be ramped gradually (starting 8kT) to match slow customer validation cycles in cosmetics/specialty sectors.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continuous process and cost optimization and development of new products, while maintaining strong relationships across the complete supply chain
- Exploring technical improvement and process optimization for better yields, product mix and energy efficiency
- Growing export markets for Dimer Acid and for the newly launched Isostearic Acid
- Exploring an opportunity to upgrade the Tocopherols and Sterols product streams when commercially viable
- Maintaining leadership in Dimer Acid via pricing strategy, timely service, quick supply, fair payment terms and product quality
- Company recommends periodic …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Trade policy] Deck flags the recent announcement of level playing tariff with the US and proposed FTA with EU/UK as augering well for the export strategy, and cites lower tariff in the US, FTA with the UK, likely FTA with the EU and recent rupee devaluation as likely to improve capacity utilization during the year, while noting macros are uncertain due to the middle east crisis.
- [Governance] Current auditors are KPMG, and the company states it has been audited by one of the Big 4 for the last 9 years; board includes independent directors Venkatraman Srinivasan, Darius Dinshaw Pandole, Sonal Vimal Ambani and Sudhin Choksey, with Nahoosh Jariwala as Managing Director and Chairman and Sumit Maheshwari as Non-Executive Director.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 63.26%, FPI 6.34%, AIF 2.02%, Public 28.38%.
- [Import substitution] Deck attributes better domestic realisation to lower imports due to supply chain constraints, indicating import competition is a key swing factor for domestic pricing.
